messages.content: Good news: my husband's vacation days were approved for July 19 through 24. Can we move from “wait and see” to actually booking the Colorado flights? I also want to be careful on seats because it looks like the Saturday flight is getting picked over.

Yes, I would move on the flights now if the fare is still Main Cabin or another changeable fare. The hold-up was the vacation approval, and that is resolved. The main risks of waiting are losing the Thursday afternoon return you wanted or ending up with worse family seating on the Saturday outbound. I would not lock in a nonrefundable mountain hotel yet, but the flights are reasonable to book now.

The Delta nonstops are still there. Saturday is late morning ATL to Denver, Thursday is an afternoon return. Main Cabin is more than the one-stop options, but basically the same premium we talked about. Basic Economy is cheaper. Outbound has maybe two seats together and one across the aisle. Return has three together farther back.

My recommendation is Delta Main Cabin now, not Basic Economy. The one-stop options save money, but they add a connection to the family travel day. Basic Economy saves more, but it weakens exactly what matters here: seat choice, flexibility, and keeping the three of you near each other. For the seat map, take the three-together row on the return even if it is farther back. For the outbound, two together plus one directly across the aisle is acceptable if that is the best remaining setup.
My husband asked if we should wait until tonight so he can look too. I don't want to rush him, but I also don't want to lose the seats.

If he has already agreed to the Saturday-to-Thursday plan and the Delta nonstop premium, I would not wait just for a second look at the same itinerary. Send him the screenshot and the all-in total before payment if you want a courtesy check. Also verify the purchase page still shows the cancellation/change terms before you click buy; if booking directly with Delta, check whether the itinerary qualifies for the 24-hour risk-free cancellation window.
For the two-and-one seat setup, who should sit where?

Put your child with one parent in the two-seat pair, and put the other parent across the aisle in the same row if possible. If the pair is window-middle, that is fine; keeping the child beside a parent matters more than getting a perfect individual seat. After ticketing, recheck the seat map periodically in case a true three-seat row opens up. I would not pay a big upgrade fee just to improve from across-the-aisle to same-side adjacent unless the current seats are scattered.
Basic Economy would save around $280 total. Still no?

Still no for this trip. With three travelers, a child, a split stay, and mountain lodging that is not fully settled, the Main Cabin flexibility and seat selection are worth more than the $280 savings. Basic Economy would be more tempting for a solo trip where you could tolerate a middle seat and fewer change options.
Okay, flights first. After that, what order should I do hotels in?

Order I’d use: 1) book the Delta Main Cabin nonstops and choose the best available seats immediately; 2) reserve a cancellable Denver room for the first two nights; 3) only hold Estes Park lodging on a cancellable or refundable rate until the room setup, parking, breakfast, fees, and cancellation deadline are clear; 4) if allowed, hold the simpler Estes backup while you wait on the better-reviewed lodge’s answers; 5) once lodging is fixed, move to rental car timing and Rocky Mountain National Park timed-entry requirements.

messages.content: Flights are done. We have two together plus one across the aisle outbound, and three together on the return. Now I need to actually choose the hotel combination.

Great. For the hotels, I’d treat Denver and Estes separately: Denver should make the first two evenings easy, while Estes should make park mornings and sleep quality easier. Send me the current options with rates and what is cancellable, and I’ll compare them as a pair.

Denver option A is downtown, about 4.4 guest rating, around $248 a night before taxes, easy restaurants, but breakfast is paid. Denver option B is a quieter suite-style place, about 4.2, $219, breakfast included, but farther from restaurants. Estes option A is the better-reviewed lodge, about 4.6, $315, breakfast not clearly listed. Estes option B is simpler two-queen, 4.1-ish, $268, breakfast included and easier parking.

Best cancellable combination from that set: downtown Denver plus the better-reviewed Estes lodge, with the simpler Estes property held as a backup if the cancellation terms allow. Denver downtown costs more after breakfast, but it reduces dinner friction and makes the one Denver day smoother. The Estes lodge is more expensive and breakfast is unresolved, but the rating gap matters more for a three-night mountain stay than for the two Denver nights.
I’m hesitating on downtown Denver because paid breakfast with a kid can get annoying fast.

That is fair. For only two Denver nights, I would not let hotel breakfast drive the whole choice unless the paid breakfast is the only practical morning option. Downtown gives you easy dinner choices after the flight day and a better base for the city day. You can handle breakfast with a nearby coffee shop, bakery, or grocery stop. The suite option wins if you expect to spend more time in the room or want the mini-kitchen more than easy evening food.
The suite property does have a mini-kitchen. But we would need to drive or rideshare for most dinners.

Then I’d keep downtown Denver as the stronger fit. The mini-kitchen is useful, but it solves breakfast while creating dinner friction. Since you’re only there two nights and want a real Denver day, restaurants nearby are more valuable than a quieter but less connected location. Request two queens, a quiet room away from elevators, and confirm any parking charge if you’ll already have the rental car.
For Estes, am I overvaluing the higher-rated lodge? Breakfast and easy parking at the simpler place sound good for park mornings.

You’re not overvaluing it if the lodge can confirm the basics. For three nights, room comfort, noise, and reliable reviews carry a lot of weight. Breakfast helps, but it does not compensate for a room that feels cramped or has weaker recent comments. The simpler property stays attractive as a backup if the lodge cannot confirm parking, a two-queen setup, cooling, or fair cancellation terms.
Can I hold both Estes places for a day or two while I ask?

Yes, if both are truly cancellable and there is no nonrefundable deposit. Set calendar reminders for each cancellation deadline, because mountain properties sometimes have earlier cutoffs than city hotels. I’d hold the better-reviewed lodge as the intended choice and the breakfast property only as insurance.
Can you give me the final order and the exact things to verify before I pay anything on the lodge?

Book in this order: downtown Denver cancellable room first; better-reviewed Estes lodge on a refundable/cancellable rate second; simpler Estes breakfast property as a temporary backup only if it can be canceled cleanly. Before paying or accepting anything nonrefundable for the lodge, verify: guaranteed two-queen room for two adults and one child, free guaranteed parking, whether breakfast exists and its hours/cost, mini-fridge, air conditioning or reliable cooling, resort or amenity fees, cancellation deadline in local time, driving time to Beaver Meadows or Fall River entrance, and whether a quiet-room request can be noted.

messages.content: I heard back from the mountain places. The better-reviewed Estes lodge can guarantee two queens and parking, but breakfast is just a paid grab-and-go. The simpler place includes breakfast, but recent reviews mention hallway noise and smaller rooms. My husband also asked if we should just stay in one Boulder-area hotel all five nights to avoid packing up.

I’d keep the split stay. Boulder for all five nights means unpacking once and more predictable restaurants, but it trades that for long drives to Rocky Mountain National Park on the days when you most want early starts. The split stay has one hotel move, but it gives you a real Denver segment and then much easier park access from Estes.
His main concern is repacking and meals. He’s not excited about changing hotels with our kid.

That concern is reasonable, but the Boulder plan mostly moves the inconvenience into the car. You would save one packing session and add repeated longer drives. Meals can still be handled with the split: Denver restaurants for the first part, then Estes restaurants plus grocery breakfast items or the lodge’s paid grab-and-go for park mornings.
So you would still choose the better lodge even without included breakfast?

Yes. The guaranteed two queens and parking resolve the biggest lodging risks, and the stronger reviews matter for three nights. The simpler property’s included breakfast is helpful, but hallway noise and smaller rooms are exactly the kind of issues that can wear on everyone after park days.
Which reservations should stay cancellable at this point?

Keep the downtown Denver reservation and the better-reviewed Estes lodge cancellable for now. Cancel the simpler Estes backup once you save the lodge’s written confirmation and confirm there is no penalty. I would not switch to Boulder unless your husband decides unpacking once matters more than shorter park mornings. Next steps: reserve the rental car, check Rocky Mountain National Park timed-entry rules, and put both hotel cancellation deadlines on the calendar.
